newsitem.title: USA: Drug kingpin gave gifts to corrupt officials - aide.
newsitem.headline: Drug kingpin gave gifts to corrupt officials - aide.

text.p: Accused drug kingpin Juan Garcia Abrego showered corrupt Mexican officials with extravagant gifts to buy protection for his cocaine empire, a former top lieutenant in the Gulf drug cartel testified on Thursday.
Francisco Perez, now in a U.S. jail, described shopping expeditions in Texas in which he would routinely spend up to $80,000 on clothes and Rolex watches for friendly police and prosecutors.

Earlier testimony in the three-week-long trial of Garcia Abrego disclosed that the alleged cartel leader paid $1.5 million a month to former Deputy Attorney General Javier Coello Trejo, who was in charge of Mexico's anti-drug efforts.

Perez said that Coello Trejo would send a courier with information about clothing sizes for him and members of his staff to Garcia Abrego's Matamoros, Mexico office, so that the items they received would be the proper fit.
Perez bought the clothes at a McAllen, Texas, shop.
"Each time, we spent $50,000 to $80,000," he said, adding that this was done on "many occasions."
Coello Trejo, now in private law practice, has told Mexican newspapers that he did not take bribes from Garcia Abrego.
Perez said certain police commanders would help Garcia Abrego move the shipments of cocaine received from the Cali drug cartel in Colombia.
"Sometimes they were there personally (to greet the planes carrying the loads)," Perez testified, adding that one police officer was given a twin-engine airplane from Garcia Abrego's personal fleet.
But the cosy relationship between the cartel and the officials ended when the two police commanders began keeping money that was supposed to go to Coello Trejo, he testified.
Coello Trejo became angry and began pressuring Garcia Abrego, Perez said.
Garcia Abrego fled in 1990 to Texas, then Chicago, but returned to Mexico late in the year after learning that he, Perez and others in the cartel had been indicted in the U.S.

He landed on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list and was finally captured on Jan. 14 in Monterrey, Mexico. Two days later, he was flown to Houston for trial, where he faces life in prison if convicted on 22 drug-related counts.

Perez said he turned himself into the U.S. authorities in August 1993 after a bitter split with Garcia Abrego, his cousin and one-time close friend, whom he accused of making fun of him and his family.
Defence attorneys alleged that Perez, a former car salesman, lied about his role in the cartel to strike back at his more powerful cousin and to get his jail sentence reduced.
